articles.title: A USPTO Docketing Change Behind the Terminal Disclaimer Collapse
articles.content:
丹尼斯·克鲁奇撰文指出，目前约10%的实用新型专利上出现了终端放弃声明（terminal disclaimers），这是自2008年以来的最低年增长率，较2023年的近22%有所下降。显而易见的双重专利权（OTDP）可能是专利法中最复杂的学说之一，但他对终端放弃声明实践的变化感到惊讶。

与此同时，联邦巡回法院正准备决定该学说的范围。Ablynx N.V.诉美国专利商标局案（No. 26-1333）中，法院将审查OTDP拒绝是否可以仅基于多个受让人带来的骚扰风险，而无需延长专利期限来证明其合理性。上个月，作者讨论了专利商标局在Ex parte Baurin案（2026年8月9日）中的回应，以及该案的上诉（2026年8月16日）。该案的进一步证据提交将于本月晚些时候（2026年9月）进行。

最初，作者试图从学说角度解释这一变化，因为近年来OTDP和终端放弃声明领域发生了许多变化。例如，In re Cellect案（2023年81 F.4th 1216）和Allergan USA, Inc.诉MSN Laboratories Private Ltd.案（2024年111 F.4th 1358）。

然而，数据表明，造成这一变化的主要原因是专利家族规模的变化。从2023年到2025年，我们看到大量续项申请、分案申请和继续前案申请（CIPs）——2023年中，这些申请占实用新型专利的40%，但如今仅占25%。续项申请（如续项）受到OTDP拒绝的概率约为原始申请的10倍。

这引发了作者对续项申请波动原因的探索。事实证明，这种波动并非由申请人引起，而是源于美国专利商标局审查政策的变化，即审查员应优先审查哪些申请。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

Terminal disclaimers now appear on about 10% of issued utility patents, the lowest annual rate since 2008 and down from almost 22% in 2023. Obviousness-type double patenting (OTDP) may be the nerdiest of our patent doctrines - but I was surprised by the transformation in terminal disclaimer practice.

The Federal Circuit meanwhile is set to decide how much of the doctrine survives. In re Ablynx N.V., No. 26-1333 (Fed. Cir.), asks whether an OTDP rejection can rest solely on the risk of harassment by multiple assignees, with no extension of patent term to justify it. Last month I wrote about the USPTO's answer to that question in Ex parte Baurin (Aug. 9, 2026), and then the appeal itself (Aug. 16, 2026). Further briefing in the case is due later this month (September 2026).

I first looked for a doctrinal explanation for the shift because there has been a lot of action with regard to OTDP and terminal disclaimers the past few years. See, for example, In re Cellect, 81 F.4th 1216 (Fed. Cir. 2023); and Allergan USA, Inc. v. MSN Laboratories Private Ltd., 111 F.4th 1358 (Fed. Cir. 2024).

But, my data point to a different cause. The biggest single driver is a change in patent family size. From 2023-2025, we saw a large bolus of continuations, divisionals and CIPs  -- making up 40% of issued utility patents in mid-2023, but represent only 25% today. Follow-on applications (such as continuations) receive OTDP rejections about 10x the rate of original filings.

This sent me on a search for the cause of the swing in continuations. It turns out that the rise (and fall) is not about applicants -- it all traces back to shifts in USPTO examination policy about which applications the examiner should pick up next.

articles.title: Strings Attached: The House Hearing on Renewing USPTO Fee Setting Authority
articles.content:
美众议院司法委员会法院、知识产权、人工智能及互联网小组委员会于2026年9月2日举行了关于续签美国专利商标局（USPTO）收费权限的听证会，此举恰逢众议院通过了将该权限延长至12月11日的临时解决方案。委员会主席达雷尔·伊萨（Darrell Issa）开场指出，12月的问题不在于是否续签，而在于以何种条款续签。这一观点与我上月向众议院工作人员提出的建议一致。

四位证人作证，均未反对续签。前局长大卫·卡波斯（David Kappos，2011年推动现行收费结构实施）建议无附加条件地延长七至八年，不附加政策条款。其他三位证人则提出了附加条件。前代理局长特雷莎·斯坦克·瑞亚（Teresa Stanek Rea）建议采用两年一轮审批制，并新增立法防护措施，包括要求专利局对专利审判局（PTAB）启动审查决定作出书面说明。协会竞争技术协会的摩根·里德（Morgan Reed）要求设定真正的到期日、恢复专利咨询委员会（PPAC）功能，并限制自主拒绝权。德州法学院教授梅丽莎·瓦瑟曼（Melissa Wasserman）则建议延长三至四年，加强财务报告结构，并由政府问责局（GAO）展开调研。

瓦瑟曼教授在该议题上具有特殊见解。她与密歇根大学教授迈克尔·弗雷克斯（Michael Frakes）合著多篇论文，通过实证研究论证，专利局的收费结构会影响其授权决定。然而，2024年由专利局委托的收费研究却未能真正回应她的研究成果。

我曾在2026年8月的一篇文章中讨论过收费延长的相关议题，指出专利复审自主拒绝权与收费结构无关，但收费权限到期却是专利局唯一必须向国会提出要求的时刻。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

The House Judiciary Subcommittee on Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet held its hearing on renewal of USPTO fee setting authority on September 2, 2026, one day after the House passed the continuing resolution that extends the authority through December 11. Chairman Darrell Issa opened with his view that the question for December is not whether to renew but on what terms. That is the same advice that I gave House staffers when I discussed the issues with them last month.

Four witnesses testified, and none argued against renewal. Former Director David Kappos (who pushed through the original fee structure in 2011) asked for a clean seven- or eight-year extension with no policy riders. The other three wanted strings. Former Acting Director Teresa Stanek Rea proposed a two-year reauthorization cycle plus new statutory guardrails, including a requirement that the Office issue written reasons for PTAB institution decisions. Morgan Reed of the Association for Competitive Technology asked for a real sunset, a functioning PPAC, and limits on discretionary denial. Professor Melissa Wasserman of Texas Law recommended three to four years, structured financial reporting, and a GAO study.

Wasserman is a particularly apt witness for this issue. She, along with Professor Michael Frakes, has published a series of articles building an empirical case that the Office's fee structure shapes its granting decisions. But the 2024 Fee Study commissioned by the USPTO dismissed her work without ever truly engaging.

I wrote about the fee extension issues in a prior August 2026 post, laying out the leverage issue: IPR discretionary denial has nothing to do with fees, but the fee sunset is the one moment when the Office must come to Congress and ask for something.
